summary: Defines an SMIv2 MIB module for managing the Rapid Spanning Tree capability from IEEE 802.1t and 802.1w for bridges between LAN segments. Its objects apply to transparent bridges and to bridges connected by other subnetworks. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Switches use a method to avoid loops in a network. This memo defines how to look at and control that method remotely.

questions: what is an edge port in rstp
how does snmp configure rapid spanning tree
subtitle: The SNMP objects for switching a bridge between classic and Rapid Spanning Tree and tuning RSTP ports.

tldr.problem: The Bridge MIB could manage the original Spanning Tree Protocol, but the IEEE 802.1t and 802.1w amendments added Rapid Spanning Tree features that had no managed objects.
tldr.mechanism: The RSTP-MIB adds two bridge-wide objects, a protocol version and a transmit hold count, and a table of six per-port objects covering edge ports, point-to-point links, protocol migration and administrative path cost.
tldr.outcome: It supplements the Bridge MIB in RFC 4188 and applies the IEEE amendments as they stood, with the working group freezing its content so later IEEE changes would not break it.

today: RFC 4318 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It supplements the Bridge MIB in RFC 4188.

sections.title: What the RSTP MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 4318 defines an SMIv2 MIB module for managing the Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP) capability. RSTP is defined by the IEEE P802.1t and P802.1w amendments to IEEE Std 802.1D-1998, for bridging between Local Area Network (LAN) segments. The objects apply both to transparent bridging and to bridges connected by subnetworks other than LAN segments.

The module is named RSTP-MIB and sits at { mib-2 134 }. Like other MIBs it is read and written through SNMP. The IANA considerations section records the assignment of that identifier.
sections.eli5: Switches that link parts of a network need a plan so messages do not loop forever. This memo describes the dials and gauges for the fast version of that plan.

sections.title: Relation to IEEE Amendments and the Bridge MIB
sections.content:
The memo lists each new object next to the IEEE clause it comes from. For instance, dot1dStpVersion maps to the ForceVersion parameter and dot1dStpTxHoldCount maps to TxHoldCount. The per-port objects map to mcheck, adminEdgePort, operEdgePort, adminPointToPointMAC, operPointToPointMAC and Path Cost. For information only it also lists the clause numbers in 802.1D-2004.

There was a concern that 802.1D-2004 could force changes to the 802.1t and 802.1w objects that were not backward compatible. The Bridge MIB working group therefore decided to freeze the technical content at a level compatible with those two amendments and leave any later updates to the IEEE 802.1 working group.

The RSTP-MIB supplements the Bridge MIB (RFC 4188), an SMIv2 update of the original BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 1493). That update added dot1dStpPortPathCost32 for IEEE 802.1t, clarified the permitted values of dot1dStpPriority and dot1dStpPortPriority, and clarified dot1dStpTimeSinceTopologyChange for bridges supporting RSTP.
sections.eli5: The memo is a map from the new settings to the pages of the official bridge rulebook that explain them. It sits next to an older bridge memo and adds to it.

sections.title: Bridge-Wide Objects
sections.content:
Two objects are added to the dot1dStp group.

dot1dStpVersion is the version of Spanning Tree the bridge is currently running. The value stpCompatible(0) means the protocol of IEEE 802.1D-1998, and rstp(2) means Rapid Spanning Tree. The default is rstp, and new values may be defined as future versions become available.

dot1dStpTxHoldCount is the value used by the Port Transmit state machine to limit the maximum transmission rate. It is an Integer32 from 1 to 10 with a default of 3.

Both are read-write, and the module says their values MUST be retained across reinitializations of the management system.
sections.eli5: There are two bridge-wide switches. One picks the old or new way of working. The other limits how often the bridge may send its messages.

sections.title: The Extended Port Table
sections.content:
The table dot1dStpExtPortTable adds one row per port by augmenting the Bridge MIB's dot1dStpPortEntry. It has six objects.

  • dot1dStpPortProtocolMigration: when running RSTP, writing true forces the port to transmit RSTP BPDUs. Any other operation has no effect and it always reads as false.
  • dot1dStpPortAdminEdgePort and dot1dStpPortOperEdgePort: the administrative and operational Edge Port parameter. Setting the admin value also sets the operational one, but the operational value becomes false on reception of a BPDU, even if the admin value is true.
  • dot1dStpPortAdminPointToPoint: forceTrue(0), forceFalse(1) or auto(2). With auto, the port counts as point-to-point if it is an Aggregator whose members are all aggregatable, or if the MAC is configured for full duplex.
  • dot1dStpPortOperPointToPoint: the operational result, re-evaluated dynamically.
  • dot1dStpPortAdminPathCost: the assigned contribution of this port to the path cost toward the spanning tree root, from 0 to 200000000. Writing 0 assigns the automatically calculated default, and the object then reads as 0.

Everything is read-write except the two operational objects, which are read-only. The module notes that an earlier object at { dot1dStp 18 } was obsoleted and should not be used.
sections.eli5: Each port on the switch gets its own settings. You can say it only connects to a single computer, whether its link is private, and how costly it is to use. The switch also reports what it actually decided.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content: The module has two groups. rstpBridgeGroup holds dot1dStpVersion and dot1dStpTxHoldCount. rstpPortGroup holds the six per-port objects. The compliance statement rstpCompliance covers device support of RSTP bridging services and makes both groups mandatory.
sections.eli5: A switch that says it supports the fast method has to provide all the bridge-wide and per-port answers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several writable objects could be misused to cause network delays and spanning tree instabilities: dot1dStpVersion, dot1dStpTxHoldCount, dot1dStpPortProtocolMigration, dot1dStpPortAdminEdgePort and dot1dStpPortAdminPathCost.

Some readable objects are sensitive too. An attacker could read dot1dStpVersion to find environments with applications or protocols sensitive to RSTP mode. dot1dStpPortAdminPointToPoint could be used to mislead an access control protocol such as 802.1x into believing only one other system is attached to a LAN segment, which could permit man-in-the-middle attacks.

The memo RECOMMENDS the SNMPv3 security features and says deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: If a stranger could change these settings, the network could slow down or get confused. They could also fool the door guard into thinking only one person is on a line. So only trusted people should be allowed to touch them.

items.label: dot1dStpPortProtocolMigration
items.desc: Write true to force RSTP BPDUs; reads as false.

items.label: dot1dStpPortOperEdgePort
items.desc: Operational Edge Port value; false after a BPDU is received.

items.label: dot1dStpPortAdminPathCost
items.desc: Assigned path cost; 0 means use the default.
